title: Small Talk: 10 ADHD Lies and How to Stop Believing Them
description: The beloved authors of Dirty Laundry break down the harmful stereotypes about people with ADHD to help you stop being your worst fear-leader, start bigging yourself up, and live your best neurodivergent life. When “ADHD wife” Roxanne Pink and neurotypical husband Richard Pink asked their community of 2.5 million what the biggest ADHD struggle is, the thousands of replies changed everything. As they learned, the real enemy isn’t productivity or focus, but the toxic ADHD core beliefs we’ve internalized. With candor and kindness, they share personal stories to highlight and reframe the 10 big lies that ADHD people believe about themselves. From “I am lazy” to “Everybody hates me” and “I quit everything I start,” Small Talk will empower ADHDers and those who love them to navigate life with compassion, humor, and hope. Whether you were diagnosed early or are new to the neurospicy community, Small Talk will change your relationship with yourself and others. title: The Small Talk and Conversation Skills Handbook: A Daily Practice Plan for Easy Openers, R
description: The question arrives at the kitchen counter, drink in hand. "So what do you do?" And the brain goes flat. Not blank; flat . There are words in there and none of them will come forward . So the answer comes out four words long, the other person has nowhere to go with it, and the whole thing is over. Then comes the drive home, and the replay, and the one better sentence that shows up three hours too late. Most books on this hand over a list of clever lines and icebreaker questions for strangers. Lines are not the problem. The problem is that nothing has been rehearsed , so the body gets there before the sentences do, and the body has never read a tip list. Sean Ashford writes a shy introvert guide that treats conversation the way it actually works: a small set of repeatable moves , drilled in the places life already puts a person, until they run without being asked . Not communication charisma. Not scripts for a business ballroom. Practice. And the rooms in this book are real rooms. School gates, gyms, waiting rooms, the office kettle, the counter where somebody is looking for a parcel. Hundreds of those a year, against maybe one professional networking function with a name badge. In The Small Talk and Conversation Skills Handbook, you will discover: The four moves that hold every conversation together, and why learning them in order matters more than learning more of them The three questions to ask about a room before opening a mouth, so a good line never lands on someone who was never available to hear it Why the Open is only ten words and about four seconds long, and the three ways in that cover almost every situation worth entering The second sentence , not hello, is where conversations die; the moves for overcoming awkwardness and keeping the floor from disappearing

title: Small Talk: Activities for Language Development in Preschool Learners
description: Small Talk: Activities for Language Development in Preschool Learners was written to fill a void for teachers who have little-to-no background in childhood language development, but wish to play an important role in language growth among preschool children. Small Talk: Activities for Language Development in Preschool Learners pushes aside drill exercises and provides caring teachers with language development activities that require easy to acquire materials/ingredients for food preparation, art and crafts, and game experiences that are designed to stimulate receptive and expressive language building experiences. Additionally, after the easy to follow activity steps, there is a listing of Small Talk Suggestions that is comprised of ideas that teachers can use to encourage conversations between themselves and their preschoolers. In this way, before, during, and after the language activity, the adult is able to provide a rich language model for the young language learner within a natural, meaningful social context. title: Small Talk: A Novel
description: For fans of Patricia Lockwood and Dolly Alderton: a hilariously moving love story hinging on one momentous evening, about a newly in-love couple who attend a lively dinner party, and what comes after Two years into their relationship, Magnus knows many things about Meredith. She is a woman of perpetually high spirits. All-American, she possesses the air of someone who has both funneled beer from a plastic pitcher down her open throat and tasted caviar straight from the fish. She never manufactures conflict to get his attention, never stiffens in anger for no good reason. And she has shown Magnus, for the first time in his romantic life, that it is possible to love someone without also despising them, even slightly. But this blissful adoration brings with it a quieter anxiety. Might she grow tired of him, of their life in his native Sweden? What does she want from him: everything or nothing at all? Tonight, Magnus and Meredith are going to a fortieth birthday party. It will be an evening like many others: people will talk too much, drink too much, and confide things they shouldn’t – about the price of the wine on the table, their obsessive marathon training, their dark pasts, marital regrets and secret aspirations. There will be indecent behavior, shifting alliances, late-night dancing and the faint, persistent sense that something larger is at stake. Because beneath all the conversations happening around the table is the one that Magnus and Meredith are not having: should this be the night they start trying for a baby, and in a relationship this happy, what the hell is going to happen next? For readers of Dolly Alderton and Jen Beagin, Small Talk is a sharp, tender and very funny novel about one couple, one night, and the moment a life might begin to change.  if(window.

description: Build key business relationships Collins Small Talk gives you the confidence to start a conversation and transition into bigger conversation topics so that you are able to build relationships, develop business partnerships and be successful in business. Learn the language to: • Meet people for the first time • Greet people in subsequent meetings • Show and receive hospitality • Deal with remote communication • End a conversation The book includes information on best practice and key phrases for students to refer to and practise saying out loud using online audio. Online audio also includes good and bad examples of authentic recordings of small talk for learners to listen to and assess. Suitable for students whose level of English is Intermediate / CEF level B1 and higher. Small Talk is part of Collins’ English for Business range of materials to help business people who need to use English frequently in their work. It is designed for people who are about to or already work for a foreign or multinational company, deal with overseas customers or travel for business.
